validated_results.title: Long-term alpha-tocopherol supplementation is associated with lower serum vascular endothelial growth factor levels.
validated_results.reason: This ATBC sub-study measured serum VEGF concentrations as a mechanistic angiogenesis biomarker in cancer-free men rather than reporting prostate cancer incidence with alpha-tocopherol supplementation.

validated_results.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
validated_results.reason: The study is an exclusively preclinical in vitro investigation of vitamin E succinate effects on androgen receptor and PSA expression in LNCaP and COS cell lines, with no human incidence data.

validated_results.title: Serum lycopene, other serum carotenoids, and risk of prostate cancer in US Blacks and Whites.
validated_results.reason: Population-based case-control study reporting serum lycopene (circulating biomarker) in relation to incident prostate cancer risk with an odds ratio and confidence interval.

extraction.comparison_type: highest versus lowest quartile of serum lycopene
extraction.population: Black and White men aged 40-79 years

sample_size.excerpt: To further explore these associations and to search for reasons prostate cancer incidence is over 50% higher in US Blacks than Whites, the authors analyzed the serum levels of individual carotenoids in 209 cases and 228 controls in a US multicenter, population-based case-control study (1986-1989) that included comparable numbers of Black men and White men aged 40-79 years.
sample_size.location: abstract; total_n derived from reported group counts 209 + 228 = 437

cases.excerpt: To further explore these associations and to search for reasons prostate cancer incidence is over 50% higher in US Blacks than Whites, the authors analyzed the serum levels of individual carotenoids in 209 cases and 228 controls in a US multicenter, population-based case-control study (1986-1989) that included comparable numbers of Black men and White men aged 40-79 years.

effect_size.excerpt: Lycopene was inversely associated with prostate cancer risk (comparing highest with lowest quartiles, odds ratio (OR) = 0.65, 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.36, 1.15; test for trend, p = 0.09), particularly for aggressive disease (comparing extreme quartiles, OR = 0.37, 95% CI: 0.15, 0.94; test for trend, p = 0.04).

confidence_interval.excerpt: Lycopene was inversely associated with prostate cancer risk (comparing highest with lowest quartiles, odds ratio (OR) = 0.65, 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.36, 1.15; test for trend, p = 0.09), particularly for aggressive disease (comparing extreme quartiles, OR = 0.37, 95% CI: 0.15, 0.94; test for trend, p = 0.04).
